Subject: Questions: prompt ephemerality, KV snapshots & backups (DPA follow-up)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. CloudCardio's privacy and security team has a few follow-ups that we need to resolve to close the DPA annex and move to procurement. High level — we need explicit retention/deletion commitments and evidence for:

- Prompt/session inputs stored by Redwood: default retention, whether customers can shorten to ephemeral, and whether prompts are written to logs/backups.
- KV cache behavior (in-memory vs persisted), snapshot cadence, and snapshot retention/purge timeline.
- System logs and audit trails: retention windows and whether deletions are irreversible and logged.
- Backups/snapshots kept for disaster recovery: retention windows, encryption, and how key rotation impacts restoreability.

Could you provide: (a) a concise table with the retention windows you commit to for each artifact above, (b) a short description of the deletion process (how it's triggered and verified), and (c) pointer to SOC2/CAIQ mapping that shows relevant controls for secure deletion and key management?

We'd like a written response by EOD Friday (2028-08-12) so legal can incorporate language into the DPA annex.

Attached is a short questionnaire from our compliance team (see Q4 on backups).

Thanks — Dana

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to get this into a short, contract-friendly format. Initial summary below; I'll loop in engineering and privacy/legal for confirmation and a one-page annex you can attach to the DPA.

Summary of proposed defaults (we can shorten/limit per-account in Dedicated/Private contracts):
- Prompt/session inputs ("prompts"): default retention = 24 hours post-session. Optional customer opt-in to 30-day retention (use-case telemetry/evals). Prompts are NOT persisted to long-term backups unless customer explicitly enables prompt logging.
- KV caches (model warm-state): active in-memory TTL ~24 hours; periodic snapshots (for warm-start/fast recovery) written to encrypted object storage every 12 hours; snapshot retention = 30 days. Snapshots are excluded from long-term backups unless customer requests DR copying.
- System/application logs & audit trails: aggregated logs retained 90 days by default (raw request logs for debugging), with finer-grained audit events available for 13 months for Enterprise customers on Dedicated plans.
- Backups (full system/service level backups): default retention = 13 months (to meet DR best practices); for Private deployments we can agree to shorter retention in the DPA annex. Backups are encrypted with customer-tenant keys where applicable; key rotation is handled via KMS and older keys are retained per key-management policy (see attachment).

Deletion process (high level):
1) Deletion mark: data is marked for deletion by the retention sweep service based on TTL/policy.
2) Secure deletion: files are removed and overwritten where supported; object-store tombstones are cleared on the next compaction; for backups we remove key-wrapping metadata and rotate keys to render copies unrecoverable if required.
3) Audit: deletion events are recorded to the audit trail (immutable append-only object) and surfaced in Console/audit exports.

I'll ask Dev to validate the snapshot cadence and the exact guarantees around key rotation effects on older backups. Rishi and Neha — can you confirm whether SOC 2 Type II evidence + CAIQ mapping will be sufficient for CloudCardio or if they require SIG-specific responses?

Attached: retention-matrix-v2.xlsx, SOC2-typeII-redacted.pdf

Thanks — adding some implementation detail from engineering so you have a clear statement for the DPA annex.

Technical details / guarantees:
- Prompts: by default, prompt payloads are buffered in transit and written to ephemeral service state; they are persisted to disk only for customers who enable "retain prompts" in Console. For "retain prompts" = off (default), prompts are dropped from persistent stores within 24 hours; ephemeral in-memory caches are GC'd within hours.
- KV cache: designed as a warm-state store. Active caches live in GPU-host local memory and are flushed to ephemeral instance-local SSD snapshots every 12 hours to allow pod restarts without cold-starts. Those instance-local snapshots are then uploaded to encrypted object storage where they are retained for 30 days and purged by our snapshot-ttl worker.
- Backups: periodic system-level backups occur nightly; snapshots used for DR are immutable copies retained for 13 months. Backups are encrypted using tenant-specific keys when available; we maintain key rotation policies: when a key is rotated, we keep wrapped keys for the older snapshots sufficient for restores within configured retention; if customer requests destruction tied to key rotation, we can remove wrapping metadata to make older backups unrecoverable per DPA language.
- Deletion verification: deletions emit an immutable audit event with a deletion ID; a secure-erase pipeline then issues a storage-layer delete and triggers compaction/garbage-collection. For object stores that don't support immediate overwrite, we treat the object as logically deleted and remove the key material to render it unrecoverable.

Caveats & options:
- For customers needing <24-hour prompt retention (e.g., strict ephemerality), we can negotiate a contract clause for session-only (no persistent writes) behavior. Note that this reduces debug traces and limits support.
- For Private deployments we can offer snapshot retention as low as 7 days if CloudCardio signs the data-reduction SLA and accepts restore risk.

Attaching a simple diagram of the snapshot flow. Happy to add a short blurb for the DPA annex describing the secure deletion steps.

-- Dev

Kimberly / Dev / Team — thanks, that is very helpful. A few follow-ups so we can finalize the DPA annex and the SOC/SIG evidence package:

1) Please confirm in writing the default values you listed (prompts = 24h; snapshot retention = 30d; logs = 90d; backups = 13 months) and indicate which of those are negotiable for Dedicated/Private customers.
2) We need explicit language that deletion is irreversible and that deletion events are recorded to an audit log that CloudCardio can export.
3) Please confirm whether key-rotation alone could prevent restores of backups that otherwise fall within retention (we need clarity for our legal team).

Next steps: if you can provide a one-page annex we can append to the DPA and the redacted SOC2 Type II report and CAIQ mapping, we will route to legal and procurement. Otherwise I can populate a draft DPA annex from your email and send back redlines.

Also — is SIG Lite acceptable or do you prefer we complete the full SIG? Our InfoSec prefers full SIG but will accept CAIQ+SOC2 if we have explicit deletion proofs and a short attestation.

Thanks — Dana
Dana Li
Privacy Manager, CloudCardio

Dana — appreciate the quick review. Confirming formally for the annex and next steps below.

Formal confirmation (for DPA annex):
- Prompts (default): 24 hours; negotiable to session-only (no persistent writes) in contract for Dedicated/Private.
- KV snapshot retention: 30 days; negotiable down to 7 days for Private deployments with signed acceptance of DR risk.
- Logs/audit trails: aggregated logs 90 days by default; extended audit exports (13 months) available for Enterprise/Dedicated.
- Backups: 13 months default; can be shortened by contract for Private deployments.

Deletion guarantees: deletions are executed by our retention sweep and secure-erase pipeline. Deletions emit an immutable audit event with a deletion ID; we will provide exportable audit records for deletion events on request (redacted if needed). Deletions that remove key wrapping metadata render backups unrecoverable; we will include the key-rotation behavior in the annex language so CloudCardio can choose the policy that meets its legal needs.

Evidence & deliverables:
- We'll provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report (attached earlier) and a CAIQ mapping document. If CloudCardio requires a full SIG, we will coordinate the SIG questionnaire — but CAIQ + SOC2 + the annex attestation is typically sufficient for most health-tech customers.

Next steps: I'll attach a draft one-page DPA annex (redlines) by EOD Monday with the table of commitments and a short deletion statement. Rishi/Neha will add legal wording for the key-rotation clause. If you prefer, send a draft annex and we'll mark it up.

Thanks,
Kimberly
